thread:
incident-bot: :bangbang: PAGER: SRE oncall (nate-sre) — elevated traffic to /v1/embeddings.batch originating from a small set of ASNs, causing tail latency and quota exhaustion for some customers. Detection rule: embed-fanout-2429991110. Dashboard: https://dash.redwood.internal/incidents/embed-fanout-2429991110

nate-sre: acked. looking at top vectors. attaching quick counts.

zara-ops: initial sniff: 2.1M requests in 30m, peak RPS 38k. Top ASNs: AS393406, AS16509, AS56041. Many requests using ephemeral key prefixes `anon_` + identical UA tokens. Batch size skew: 256-1024 predominantly.

liu-eng: seeing cache amplification on edge kvcache when batch split enabled — large splits are causing upstream fanout to storage and high tail. Also some 502s from batch worker pool due to OOM on kv-merge.

nate-sre: mitigation proposal: A) enforce per-key short-term batch cap, B) deploy CAPTCHA challenge on suspicious traffic to embeddings.batch, C) temporarily disable automatic batch-splitting for anonymous keys, D) soft ban offending IP prefixes for 10m. Proceeding with A and C first.

zara-ops: applying per-key caps now: `rlctl set --route /v1/embeddings.batch --scope api_key --burst 20 --rate 120/min --id rl-2429`

rate-limit result (captcha-bot): applied rl-2429, matched 157k keys, throttled 312k requests in 90s.

liu-eng: toggling batch-split off for anon keys: ```rbctl set route /v1/embeddings.batch --disable_auto_split_for_prefix=anon_ --commit``` will roll in 30s. Also bumped worker mem limit to prevent immediate OOMs.

priya-ps: prepping comms. We should note that enterprise allowlists won't be affected. I'll coordinate with @cory-sales to notify impacted customers.

cory-sales: pinged 3 customers, two on phone already. BetaCorp reports many of their bulk jobs failing; they run with a verified key but use parallelism settings that look like abuse. Asking for temporary quota bump.

nate-sre: allowing verified enterprise keys via allowlist: `rbctl allow-key --key=prod-VC-BETACORP --routes=/v1/embeddings* --reason "verified enterprise"`

liu-eng: starting CAPTCHA rollout for suspicious flows via edge WAF challenge. Rule: match UA patterns, anon key prefix, and ASN list. Config snippet: ```wafctl create challenge --id wf-captcha-2429 --match "http.request.uri contains '/v1/embeddings.batch' and http.request.headers['Authorization'] contains 'anon_' and origin.asn in (393406,16509,56041)" --challenge_type captcha --duration 10m``` Applying in staged regions (EU, APAC) first.

captcha-bot: wf-captcha-2429 active in EU. Matched 48.2k, challenged 44.6k, passed 1.1k (likely legit), failed 43.5k.

zara-ops: early effect: total RPS down 72% in EU, global embed batch 5xxs down from 3.6% -> 0.9% in 10min. However median latency for legitimate customers still up ~30% due to queueing.

nate-sre: temporarily reconfigured route to enforce a global per-key daily batch quota for anon keys: `rbctl quota set --prefix anon_ --route /v1/embeddings.batch --daily_batches 50 --id q-2429` — this'll limit further abuse while we evaluate.

priya-ps: sent targeted note to affected customers: "We're mitigating an automated bulk-access pattern affecting embeddings.batch. Actions taken: targeted throttles, CAPTCHA on suspicious flows, temporary per-key caps. Verified customers are allowlisted. If you still see issues, reply here or open an urgent support ticket."

cory-sales: BetaCorp accepted a temporary scoped quota increase after verification; jobs resubmitted successfully.

liu-eng: relevant deployment logs: ```[2026-03-15T08:11:21Z] waf: wf-captcha-2429 matched req id=xyz123 src=1.2.3.4 asn=393406 challenged
[2026-03-15T08:12:02Z] rbctl: quota q-2429 applied for prefix=anon_
[2026-03-15T08:14:45Z] workers: mem-limit bump applied for embed-pool-5, drain delay=20s```

nate-sre: we should avoid a full disable of embeddings.batch; that harms UX for legit high-volume users. Plan: maintain allowlist + challenge + per-key caps for next 2 hours, reassess.

zara-ops: creating temporary ip-blackhole list for worst offenders: `netctl block --prefix 203.0.113.0/24 --duration 10m --reason embed-scrape-2429` (applied in APAC). First block matched 7k flows, reduced load significantly.

priya-ps: customer impact summary so far (preliminary): ~9 customers had >15% job failures; 2 had >30%. We offered mitigation credits and priority support. No PII or key compromise detected.

nate-sre: preparing handoff to @oncall-next in 20m. Open actions for next oncall:
- Monitor captcha pass-rate & tune false-positive threshold (liu)
- Review ASN blocklist and consider ASN throttles vs IP blackholing (zara)
- Confirm KV cache behavior with batch-split off (liu)
- Draft post-incident customer-facing summary (priya + cory)

oncall-next: will pick up. please paste final counters before handoff.

zara-ops: final counters before handoff: total requests window=30m: 2.1M, challenged by CAPTCHAs=295k, blackholed flows=98k, rate-limited requests=412k, error-rate (5xx) baseline->current = 0.7% -> 1.1% (mostly retries), median latency for verified keys 180ms -> 240ms, for anon keys 420ms -> 1.1s.

incident-bot: Reminder: handoff at 2429991300 UTC. Use `/incident update` to append notes. Thread will be auto-archived after handoff.

nate-sre: leaving detailed runbook snippet here before I go:---
RUNBOOK (short):
1) If spike from anon keys: apply per-prefix quota and per-key short-term caps (rbctl quota/rlctl).
2) If traffic source is clustered by ASN: consider ASN-level throttle instead of full IP blocks.
3) Use WAF challenge (captcha) on suspicious flows; use short windows and monitor pass rates.
4) Allowlist verified enterprise keys to avoid service impact.
5) Only disable embeddings.batch globally as last resort; prefer prefix-scoped controls.
---

oncall-next: acknowledged, taking over at 2429991300. I'll hold monitoring for 2h and escalate if aggregate RPS rises >20% of current.

priya-ps: sending final PS note to affected list. Thanks for the quick coordination everyone :thumbsup:

nate-sre: handing off and signing out.
